title: Jumping on an Open Number Line

steps.body: An open number line turns addition into jumps: big friendly jumps of hundreds and tens, landing where the answer lives.
steps.narration: An open number line turns addition into jumps: big friendly jumps of hundreds and tens, landing where the answer lives.

commonLandings.feedback: One hop is only +10 — the sum needs all three ten-jumps to reach 497.

widget.missFeedback: Each hop is 10. From 467, 3 hops land on 497.
widget.successFeedback: Landed on 497 — the line carried the running total through every hop.

predict.prompt: Jumping +10 three times from 467: where do you land?
predict.reveal: Each hop adds ten: 477, 487, 497 — thirty in all.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2b open line.
invariants: Trading between places changes the FORM of a quantity, never its value — the model and the number must stay equal for g2b open line.
misconceptions: Treating a trade as adding or removing amount instead of renaming the same total.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the blocks stop matching the written number?

explanationVariants: Each hop is a whole ten.

commonErrors.feedback: That hopped by ONES; each jump here is a whole ten.
One hop too many — count the tens jumps exactly.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Line the places up — hundreds with hundreds, tens with tens, ones with ones — and work one column at a time.

hints: Big jumps first, small jumps after.

widget.prompt: You want to add 199 + 350 in your head. Which tool fits?

options.label: An open number line with friendly jumps
options.feedback: Correct — jumping +100s then +10s keeps a running total you can see, ideal for adding in your head.

options.label: Trading blocks one cube at a time
options.feedback: Cube-by-cube counting works but wastes the big friendly jumps this problem offers.

options.label: Writing the word form first
options.feedback: Word form renames the number; it does not move the calculation forward.

options.label: Memorizing the answer
options.feedback: There is no fact table for three-digit sums; strategies, not memory, carry these.

hints: Big jumps first, small jumps after.
The last landing is the answer.
